title: Sectionwise pushout for completed constant coefficient maps
statement: For a prime l, finite extensions E and F of Q_l, an algebra map i : E → F, a scheme W, and every pro-etale object U of W, the square of commutative rings formed by the constant E-to-F map, the two constant-to-completion maps, and the normalized completed coefficient map is a pushout. The maps are the coefficient maps of [def-pur-constant-scalar-tensor-data], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), together with the finite-free completed scalar comparison; basis-and-reduction construction of the ordinary coefficient tensor comparison.

proof.text: Choose an integral basis and the positive ramification relation, then lift them to the coefficient universe. The specified constant-sheaf basis gives a bijection from tuples of constant source sections to constant target sections, whose columns are the constant basis vectors. Evaluating the finite-product comparison supplies the tuple coordinates.

Use the adic basis construction and its injectivity and surjectivity to obtain the analogous finite-sum bijection on completed sections with the same constant columns. The quotient-presentation isomorphisms induce completion isomorphisms. Their finite-projection identities identify the adic scalar map with completedCoefficientMap. Naturality of constantCommuteCompose and the quotient cone identify both constant-to-completion maps. Thus these ring isomorphisms transport the two normalized finite-sum bijections to the exact section rings and maps in the statement.

For a commuting square of commutative rings, suppose a finite list of vectors is a basis on the constant side and its image is a basis on the completed side. Regard the two finite-sum bijections as linear equivalences. They define bases; the canonical tensor multiplication map sends the base-changed first basis to the second, hence is bijective. Turn it into an algebra equivalence and transport the canonical commutative-ring tensor-product pushout through this equivalence. The argument uses no nontriviality hypothesis, so also covers zero section rings and the empty object.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof from the existing normalized finite-basis APIs. Private proved helpers establish sectionwise finite-sum bijectivity and its tensor-pushout consequence; no new proof obligations.
